scopeOfTheClaim: R1 only: authorship of the compliance-path files below. Correctness is for CI (R4) and the CTO review (R2).
whatTheChangeActuallyDoes: Migration 0055 (+rollback): leave_balances (person NOT NULL FK CASCADE — documented deviation from the generic SET NULL denorm convention since an allowance cannot outlive its holder; year 2000-2100; allowance_days>=0; unique person+year; branch/zone route-stamped denorms SET NULL per the 0044 choice-8 precedent with no scope trigger so suite 94 is untouched) with SELECT/INSERT(col-list)/UPDATE/DELETE grants to directus_app and PUBLIC revoked; ownership + bootstrap-role preconditions per the 0042 pattern. Suite 55: rerun no-op, shape (allowance write/duplicate-year refusal/negative refusal/adjust/withdraw; probe holders use fixed ids and stay because people is retention-managed, AFC-295 — household stays NULL so the 85 emptiness pin never sees them), grants (SELECT, INSERT+UPDATE+DELETE, PUBLIC-empty), live down/up cycle with restrict_violation refusal while rows exist. No existing suite touched: parents (people/branches/zones) are never dropped in-harness. Phase 2 (used/remaining vs leave_requests, request-dialog integration, team view) is explicitly out of this packet and waits on AFC-842.
whatThisFileIs: An R1 authorship claim, and nothing else. It says who wrote the compliance-path files below and on which issue. It asserts nothing about whether they are correct, and it carries no reviews[] entry.
doesNotClaimR2: There is no reviews[] entry here and there will not be one from me. R2 wants a named reviewer who is not the author. CTO R2 requested on the AFC-854 thread before landing.
notClaimedPaths: Non-compliance paths in the same packet (shared COLLECTIONS + role-matrix entry mirroring session_activities hands + leave schemas, leave.ts working-day counter, four leave-balances API routes with person scope-gating and zone-from-person stamping, time-off.vue with allowance book + working-day calculator, Church Office nav entry, time-off contract) need no claim and land with the R2 verdict.
